name: sdd:resolve-task-paths: reads the Task Workflow keys
prompt: Invoke the sdd:resolve-task-paths skill for this project. Report the resolved PRD path, the specs directory, the tasks directory, whether a nested spec repo was detected, and which persistence model this project's documents follow. Do not write any files.

graders.why: it must resolve the PRD from the Task Workflow section
the specs directory is one of the keys it exists to resolve
the tasks directory is one of the keys it exists to resolve
it must answer the question, not repeat it; the prompt already says 'spec repo was detected'
it must never fall back to that path; the rules forbid it
the fixture's CLAUDE.md declares no Spec Model, so the default has to fire and be named. A skill that reports the paths and goes quiet about the model leaves every command downstream to assume one

a model that was defaulted and one that was chosen should produce the same behaviour and a different report. The owner cannot tell whether the project ever decided this unless the skill says which happened
